main_body: A wooden display rack of three stacked horizontal wooden bands (top plank rows 0-4, a shelf with goods rows 7-16, bottom plank rows 19-23) joined by thin posts. The gaps between the bands are open.
top_band: none. At x=15 the scan shows only a 1-row lighter line (row 1, L=98) over the same brown face (L=64), so it is a rim, not a top surface. The middle shelf has a 1-row lighter edge at row 12 and no horizontal surface above it.
evidence: Every band is drawn face-on. The top plank is rows 0-4 in nearly one brown tone (L 60-98 then 64) with only a 1-row highlight, which is a rim. The middle shelf shows goods inside a face-on frame, with no seen-from-above surface. The bottom plank is also a vertical front band. Nothing reads as a top surface, so this is a front elevation of a shelf rack and fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The wood uses about 5 brown steps (#3d220c, #633712, #6f4725, #885a26, #b77541) with grain dots. The outline is a tinted dark brown and none of the dark edge pixels are neutral. Flat-fill coverage is 0% and median colours per tile is 18, against 17 and 20 in the references. The total of 18 distinct colours is below the references' 38-40, but the piece is small, so this is acceptable. It sits comfortably beside the stall and well references.
